title: 5 Tips for Resuming Running Training after Illness

blocks.text: By : Zaytouni

Running is an excellent way to maintain both physical and mental health, but what happens when an illness forces us to interrupt our running routine? Returning to training after a period of illness requires attention and a step-by-step approach to ensure the body’s well-being. Here are five useful tips for safely getting back into running.

Winter running can present significant challenges. Aside from being uncomfortable physically, cold weather raises the danger of illness, which might compromise your developed training form. Running enthusiasts understand how challenging it can be to break the flow of their training, particularly when they are at their best. Because of this, we provide you with five suggestions on how to safely return to training following a time of illness.

1. Recognize the Type of Disease
Prior to anything else, it's critical to recognize the nature of your sickness. Generally speaking, symptoms that are not related to the throat, like a runny nose, sore throat, or headache, do not always mean that training must stop. In some circumstances, these symptoms can even be reduced with very (!) mild and tailored training (training with a cold). If you have chosen to stop training because of these symptoms, you can start back up as soon as you're feeling well again.

It is crucial to stop exercise and take extra measures if you experience any symptoms below the neck, such as muscle discomfort, respiratory inflammation, bronchitis, coughing, vomiting, diarrhea, or a fever higher than 37 degrees. Before you resume running training, wait until you've finished the recommended treatments, make sure you restore lost energy and nutrients, and give yourself a day off for every day that you have a fever.

2. Remembrance and Prudence
We are aware that you are eager to resume your outside running. To avoid the chance of a relapse, you must, however, exercise patience and not rush the healing process. The body need more time to heal after a sickness, sometimes up to two weeks. Wait four to five days after recovering fully from a fever before resuming your running activities.

It is not advisable to run when feverish because this increases the chance of going into the "open window" phase. In this stage, the body is unable to respond to germs and viruses in a way that strengthens the immune system. The window is available not only during sickness but also following vigorous exercise since physical activity compromises immunity.

3. Gradual Comeback
It's time to go back into training after the sickness has passed. To return to your pre-illness level, nevertheless, will most likely take some time. To enable the body to revert to its typical training standards, physical activity must be progressively resumed during the first week, albeit at a lesser intensity. Begin with a 7–10 day "buffer" phase during which you progressively boost the time and intensity while closely monitoring your body's cues. The following are some things to remember:

Skip the long runs and intervals.
Choose recuperation and light endurance runs.
Adapt the distance or workout time as needed.
For the purpose of restoring muscle and joint mobility, engage in stretching, strength, and flexibility exercises.
Think about substitute sports like yoga, cycling, and swimming.

4. Keep an eye on your workouts
When you start jogging again, it's important to pay close attention to how your body reacts. Don't disregard any discomfort; instead, pay attention to cues like weariness and tightness in your muscles. It is preferable to lower the training intensity during the first sessions if heart rate and perceived effort are higher than normal. It is best to halt training and see a doctor again if you have symptoms like nausea, dizziness, or fever.

5. Consumption and Healing
The phase of recuperation holds equal significance to the actual training. Remember to honor your body's required recuperation periods. To help muscles mend and recover, it's essential to get adequate sleep and give yourself days of active rest. A thorough recuperation lowers the chance of overtraining and makes the transition back to physical activity more successful.

A balanced diet is also necessary for recuperation from an illness since it replenishes nutrients and energy that have been lost. Adding a multivitamin to the diet might be extremely helpful, particularly if the sickness has lowered nutritional intake or impacted appetite. By giving the body the essential nutrients, this assistance can help to boost immunity and encourage a speedy recovery.

title: Leylah Fernandez takes down 5th seed Qinwen Zheng to reach Qatar
summary: In Rotterdam, Raonic into quarters while Auger-Aliassime and Shapovalov lose

blocks.text: In Rotterdam, Raonic into quarters while Auger-Aliassime and Shapovalov lose
On Wednesday, Leylah Fernandez of Canada defeated China's fifth-seeded player Qinwen Zheng 7-5, 6-3 to move to the Qatar Open quarterfinals.
In the opening set, Fernandez overcame a 5-3 deficit, then in the second set, she secured her third break in four opportunities and held on to win the match in 92 minutes.
In the career series between the Grand Slam finalists who are 21 years old, Fernandez has advanced to 2-0.
The Canadian won her second of three WTA titles in the second round of Monterrey 2022 after defeating Zheng 6-1, 4-6, 7-6 (3).
Fernandez, who was as low as No. 95 in July yet entered the tournament, is winning for the first time this year against a top-10 opponent.
Auger-Aliassime falls to Rublev
Canada's Felix Auger-Aliassime dropped his second-round match at the ABN Amro Open tennis tournament against Russia's Andrey Rublev losing 6-3, 6-7 (6), 5-7 in Rotterdam, Netherlands.
The Montreal native had 20 aces and 42 winners in the two-hour 33-minute match.
However, he had 22 unforced errors to just 12 from Rublev, along with five double faults to his opponents' two.
The 23-year-old Auger-Aliassime won the tournament back in 2022, one of the four he was victorious in that year
Raonic rides powerful serve
Canadian veteran Milos Raonic advanced to the quarterfinals earlier with a 6-4, 6-4 upset of eighth seed Alexander Bublik of Kazakhstan.
The 33-year-old Raonic, a former world No. 3 from Thornhill, Ont., scored a key break to go up 3-2 in the second set and kept Bublik at bay the rest of the way with his powerful serve.
Five of Raonic's 12 aces came after that break, including three straight to go up 5-3 and another to set up match point in the final game.
Nadal pulls out of Qatar Open
Rafael Nadal put off his return to the tennis tour because he isn't yet healthy enough to play, announcing Wednesday that he will sit out next week's Qatar Open.

"I would have loved to play in Doha, where the tournament team, as well as the amazing Qatar fans have always supported me greatly. Unfortunately I am not ready to compete and I won't be able to come to Doha where I really wanted to be and play again after that unforgettable win in 2014," Nadal wrote on social media. "I will focus on keep working to be ready for the exhibition in Las Vegas and the amazing Indian Wells tournament."
The 37-year-old Spaniard is scheduled to participate in an exhibition match with Carlos Alcaraz on March 3, then head to Indian Wells, Calif., for the hard-court tournament there next month.

Nadal played in three matches at the Brisbane International in early January — his first competitive action in nearly a full year — but then pulled out of the Australian Open and hasn't been back since.
He hurt his hip flexor during the Australian Open in 2023, and eventually needed surgery, missing the rest of last season.
Nadal has indicated this year might be the last of his career, and he's pointed to the French Open — where he won 14 of his 22 Grand Slam titles — as his focus.

title: 5 Most Effective Gym Workouts for Weight Loss
summary: Navigating the path to optimal weight-loss success through the vast world of workouts can be quite a puzzle. The term "workout" encompasses a wide range of activities, spanning from strength and muscle-building exercises...

blocks.text: Navigating the path to optimal weight-loss success through the vast world of workouts can be quite a puzzle. The term "workout" encompasses a wide range of activities, spanning from strength and muscle-building exercises to cardio and mobility workouts. It's not just about knowing which exercises to do; it's about figuring out the best way to do them. The options are endless—straight sets, super sets, HIIT intervals, and circuits, leaving you feeling like you're back at square one, lost in the confusion. Allow me to guide you through the process. I crafted a list of the top five most effective gym workouts for weight loss, so listen up.

These routines cover a range of exercises, from strength and muscle-building movements to activities that will elevate your heart rate, ensuring a swift and efficient calorie burn. Here's the breakdown: The initial workouts focus on establishing a foundation through strength and muscle building. Next, you'll target your core, the fundamental support system for the human body. Finally, we'll conclude with a refreshing, heart-pounding exercise to maximize your weight-loss potential. All reps stay higher in volume; the rest periods are short, never exceeding 60 seconds.

Feel free to spice up your routine by incorporating the provided exercise variations. Begin with classic straight sets, and in your next workout, explore the dynamic realms of intervals or embrace the intensity of HIIT-style circuits. Keep the volume higher, the rep ranges, and the rest periods shorter. Unleash your creativity, and let it shine through your workout choices!
Workout #1 Renegade Rows

Renegade rows offer diverse exercises ideal for weight loss, incorporating full-body, high-intensity movements that challenge stability and muscle endurance. While primarily targeting the lats and upper back, renegade rows engage the abs for stability. This dynamic exercise combines elements of dumbbell rows and planks, concluding with the anti-rotation challenge of pull-throughs.
1. Renegade Rows
The standard renegade row serves as an excellent foundation. Once you try it, you'll recognize its effectiveness in delivering a challenging workout while supporting your weight-loss goals.

Start in a plank position with your hands under your shoulders. Lift one hand, pulling your elbow to the ceiling in a strong rowing motion while balancing on the other arm. Alternate sides, maintaining stability and squeezing your core. Complete three sets of 12 to 15 reps per side with 60 seconds of rest between sets. Want to turn it up a notch? Hold a five-second plank between your rows.
2. Renegade Rows with Pushups

Pairing renegade rows with pushups creates an excellent upper-body exercise to drive weight loss, build strength, and improve muscle endurance. Oh, and stability—we can't overlook that physical quality! In addition to focusing on your lats, upper back, and abs, you'll be working your chest, shoulders, and triceps.

Start in a plank position with your hands under your shoulders. Lift one hand, pulling your elbow to the ceiling in a strong rowing motion while balancing on the other arm. Alternate sides, maintaining stability and squeezing your core. Next, lower your body to the height of the dumbbells, and push back up, executing a pushup. Perform three sets of 8 to 12 reps with 60 seconds of rest between sets.
3. Renegade Rows with Mountain Climbers

Upper back and lat strength? Check. Abs and shoulder stability? Check. Dynamic core action? Check. Performing mountain climbers after renegade rows amplifies the fat-burning potential of your workout. It adds a high-rep, high-intensity element to maximize your calorie burn and overall effectiveness.

To execute a renegade row with a mountain climber, start in a high plank position with your hands gripping dumbbells under your shoulders, and plant your feet hip-width apart. Perform a row with one dumbbell, keeping the elbow close to the body, then switch to the other arm. Next, perform mountain climbers by driving one knee toward the chest, switching legs quickly in a running motion. Maintain core engagement throughout. Complete desired reps or time duration with controlled movements. Complete three sets of eight to 12 reps with 60 seconds of rest between sets. Knock out five mountain climbers per side with each repetition of renegade rows per side.
Workout #2 Lunge Variations
1. Walking Lunges

Elevate the impact of standard lunges with walking lunges, which add a dynamic element by having you move over a specified distance or complete a set number of reps, intensifying the workout. Feel free to enhance the challenge by incorporating weights such as dumbbells, kettlebells, barbells, or even medicine balls. Adding weight accelerates calorie burning and promotes strength and definition in key muscle groups like the quads, hamstrings, and glutes.

Start with your feet hip-width apart. Step forward with your right foot, ensuring your knee aligns with the ankle, and lower the back knee above the ground. Push through your right foot to bring the left foot forward into the next lunge. Alternate legs with each step, maintain an upright posture, engage your core for stability, and maintain a smooth, controlled movement. Repeat for the desired number of reps or distance. Perform three sets of 12 to 20 reps per side with 40 to 60 seconds of rest between sets.
2. Alternating Reverse Lunges
Alternating reverse lunges keep you moving; if you're driving, your metabolism works. Forward lunges emphasize the quads, while reverse lunges target the hamstrings and glutes of the rear leg.

Begin with your feet hip-width apart. Step back with your right foot, keeping the left knee above the ankle. Keep the right knee slightly above the ground. Push up with your left and right foot to return to the starting position, then repeat with the left foot stepping back. Alternate legs in a controlled manner, maintaining a smooth and steady rhythm. Complete three sets of 12 to 20 reps per side with 40 to 60 seconds of rest between sets.
3. Pendulum Lunges

This is the ultimate strength- and metabolism-boosting lunge exercise. A pendulum lunge combines the benefits of both reverse and forward lunges while challenging your stability and coordination. Get ready to feel the "burn" in your legs.

Begin with your feet hip-width apart. Step back with your right foot, keeping the left knee above the ankle. Keep the right knee slightly above the ground. Next, push off the ground with your right foot, and bring the right leg through into a forward lunge. Continue the pendulum-like motion with the right leg for the prescribed reps or time, and then repeat with the left leg. Perform three sets of eight to 12 reps per side with 60 seconds of rest between sets. (Your "eight to 12 reps per side" is 16 to 24 total reps of work, increasing the intensity of this lunge variation."
Workout #3 Dumbbell Bench Press

To optimize your workouts for weight loss, integrating compound lifts is critical. These exercises engage multiple muscle groups simultaneously, intensifying calorie burn and muscle building. Dumbbell bench press workouts epitomize this strategy, offering compound lift benefits and stability for enhanced muscle engagement. Plus, they provide flexibility to adjust the intensity by varying weights or movement options.

title: أموال و"فيلات" لأبطال إفريقيا.. على كم حصل كل لاعب إيفواري؟
summary: حصل لاعبو منتخب كوت ديفوار ومديرهم الفني إيميرس فاييه على مكافآت مادية مجزية وفيلات، خلال مراسم احتفالية في القصر الجمهوري بمناسبة تتويجهم بكأس أمم إفريقيا التي أقيمت على أرضهم. وتغلب منتخب "الأفيال" على نيجيريا 2-1 في ا...

blocks.text: حصل لاعبو منتخب كوت ديفوار ومديرهم الفني إيميرس فاييه على مكافآت مادية مجزية وفيلات، خلال مراسم احتفالية في القصر الجمهوري بمناسبة تتويجهم بكأس أمم إفريقيا التي أقيمت على أرضهم. وتغلب منتخب "الأفيال" على نيجيريا 2-1 في المباراة النهائية، الأحد، حاصدا اللقب القاري للمرة الثالثة. وحصل كل فرد من أفراد الفريق على 50 مليون فرنك إفريقي (نحو 82 ألف دولار)، وفيلا بنفس القيمة. في المقابل، حصل المدرب فاييه على 100 مليون فرنك إفريقي (حوالي 164 ألف دولار)، إثر تغيير لافت أحدثه بعد أن حل بدلا من الفرنسي جان لوي غاسيه المقال من منصبه في منتصف البطولة، بعد الهزيمة الثقيلة صفر-4 في دور المجموعات أمام غينيا الاستوائية. كما تم منح جميع اللاعبين الوسام الوطني، وهو أعلى وسام في البلاد. وقال الرئيس الإيفواري الحسن واتارا للاعبين: "جلبتم السعادة لجميع الإيفواريين. برافو. برافو".

blocks.text:
Following Sunday's exciting Africa Cup of Nations final, football players from Ivory Coast and Nigeria are receiving cash, residences, and honours.
According to the presidency, each member of Ivory Coast's victorious team would receive $82,000 (£65,000) in compensation as well as a property of comparable value.
"You have brought happiness to all Ivorians, bravo, bravo," the pan-African tournament's host nation, Ivory Coast, President Alassane Ouattara, exclaimed.
Nigeria was greeted like heroes as well.

President Bola Tinubu is generously rewarding the Super Eagles, despite the fact that their 2-1 loss in the championship game devastated the team's millions of supporters both at home and abroad.
The Member of the Order of the Niger is one of the highest distinctions bestowed upon members of the Nigerian team. Additionally, the president is gifting each of them a plot of property close to Abuja, the capital, as well as an apartment.
According to local media, South Africa, who finished in third place, will also get roughly $52,000 for each player.
What kind of cash remuneration Nigerian players are expected to get from the state coffers is unclear.

However, all of the benefits mentioned above are on top of the standard prize money awarded by the Africa Cup of Nations, which they claim has increased by 40% since the previous competition.
This implies that the four teams that advanced to the quarterfinals will each receive $1.3 million, while the winners, Ivory Coast, will receive $7 million, Nigeria, the runner-up, will receive $4 million, and South Africa, the semi-finalist, will receive $2.5 million.
The Africa Cup of Nations saw the most viewers in its 67-year existence this year, largely due to increased coverage, commercial arrangements, and social media excitement. Global viewership is estimated to have reached around two billion people.

Analysts anticipate that more starting spots for African teams at upcoming World Cups will result from the world's recognition of Africa's flair for football.
Africa currently holds nine World Cup berths compared to Europe's thirteen, even though the number of Fifa-affiliated countries on these two continents is almost equal.
The national teams of Africa have previously complained about not receiving their bonuses and salary.
The Cameroonian team that captured the hearts of people all over the world with their World Cup quarterfinal performance against England in 1990 waited more than 30 years to receive the mansions they were promised, by which time their captain had passed away.
South African football players won a pay dispute at the Fifa Women's World Cup last year after boycotting a game in protest. Their hurriedly put together stand-ins had included a 13-year-old girl
